claims.text: GUARD: the run reported on EXACTLY the frozen nodes, or say what moved.
claims.why: Function checks extra and missing nodes and returns error strings.

claims.text: A runner is injectable, and a gate is a subprocess whose output is parsed; either could in principle report a node that is not in the frozen set (a parser that matched too loosely, a runner that expanded a selector).
claims.why: No code in this chunk defines runner or gate implementation; claim refers to external design.

claims.text: A result computed over a set that is not the declared one is not the measurement that was declared, so it is refused rather than reported.
claims.why: Function returns error string if extra or missing nodes exist.

claims.text: ``verified`` is True only when every FAIL_TO_PASS node was PROVEN not to pass and every PASS_TO_PASS node passed. Anything else is either an invalid task or an unobtainable verdict, and ``reasons`` says which.
claims.why: judge_before_state sets verified=True only when no reasons; otherwise sets invalid or unrunnable and provides reasons.

claims.text: The declaration, written into the receipt so a reader can check that what was measured is what was declared -- and so the gate can refuse a task whose lists moved after it was verified.
claims.why: to_dict includes selection and selection_digest fields.

claims.text: Pure: turn before-state node statuses into a verdict about the TASK. Three separate refusals, in this order: 1. NO VERDICT (``not_run``) -> ``unrunnable``. 2. A claimed FAIL_TO_PASS node that PASSED, was SKIPPED, or is MISSING -> ``invalid``. 3. A claimed PASS_TO_PASS node that did not pass -> ``invalid``.
claims.why: Code checks unknown first (unrunnable), then bad_f2p (invalid), then bad_p2p (invalid) in that order.

claims.text: Pure: ``(outcome, reason, fixed, unfixed, regressed)`` after the change. PRECEDENCE: could_not_run > regressed > not_fixed > fixed.
claims.why: Code checks unknown first (could_not_run), then regressed, then unfixed, else fixed.

claims.text: ``could_not_run`` first, because an unattributed node is an unknown and an unknown must never be read as a verdict.
claims.why: Code returns OUTCOME_COULD_NOT_RUN immediately if unknown nodes exist.

claims.text: ``regressed`` next, because a change that breaks the regression set is reported as breaking it EVEN IF it also turned every FAIL_TO_PASS green -- collapsing those two into one boolean is exactly how a plausible-looking bad patch gets promoted.
claims.why: Code checks regressed after unknown, before unfixed.

claims.text: Takes the frozen :class:`Selection`, NOT the task dict, and that is the structural half of the immutability rule: once a selection is frozen there is no code path left that can consult the task for node ids again, so a task mutated mid-evaluation (by a runner, a gate, or a caller holding the same dict) cannot change what is measured.
claims.why: _run_lists takes selection parameter, not task dict; uses selection.fail_to_pass and selection.pass_to_pass.

claims.text: Two invocations on purpose: a collection error in one list must not turn the other list into ``not_run`` (measured -- one uncollectable node id aborts the whole invocation with exit 4 and nothing else runs).
claims.why: No code in this chunk shows behavior of runner on collection error or exit code 4.

claims.text: The selection is frozen FIRST, before the worktree exists and long before any candidate bytes are applied, and the after-state is run against that same frozen object -- so the thing being measured cannot be influenced by the thing being measured.
claims.why: Code chunk does not show the freezing step; only shows that selection is used later.

claims.text: The before-state is measured every time, in the same tree the after-state is measured in. It is never read from a stored receipt here, because a receipt is a claim about a tree that may no longer exist.
claims.why: Code chunk does not show before-state measurement; only partial function definition.

claims.text: ``use_reference`` evaluates the task's OWN fix commit (``reference_revision``) instead of a candidate patch. That is how a corpus task is validated: a task whose own reference patch does not produce ``fixed`` is not a task.
claims.why: Code chunk does not show how use_reference is used; only parameter declaration.

observations.what: guard_selection computes declared and observed sets from selection and passed node dicts; returns error strings if mismatched.
BeforeState.to_dict includes selection_digest field, but selection_digest is not a field of BeforeState; it accesses selection.digest directly.
judge_before_state checks unknown nodes first; if any, returns unrunnable BeforeState without checking bad_f2p or bad_p2p.
judge_before_state uses PROVEN_NOT_PASSING constant; not defined in this chunk.
judge_before_state uses STATUS_PASSED, STATUS_MISSING, NO_VERDICT constants; not defined in this chunk.
judge_after_state returns regressed nodes even if some f2p nodes are unfixed; precedence is enforced as documented.
_run_lists runs f2p first, then p2p only if selection.pass_to_pass is non-empty; p2p statuses are taken from the second run.
evaluate_change is incomplete; ends mid-function at line ~1004.
